q: Lubrication of the gauge face of the outer rail on sharp curves is resorted to in order to:

options.A: Improve the electrical contact between the wheel and the rail
options.B: Increase the adhesion of the locomotive wheels
options.C: Prevent the derailment of trains on the curve
options.D: Reduce the wear of the rail gauge face and of the wheel flanges

e: On sharp curves the flange of the outer wheel presses hard against the gauge face of the outer rail; lubricating that face reduces friction, and so reduces wear of both the rail gauge face and the wheel flanges.

q: Anti-creep anchors are fitted to the rails in the track in order to:

options.A: Hold the rails down against lifting by passing trains
options.B: Resist the longitudinal movement (creep) of the rails by anchoring them to the sleepers
options.C: Maintain the correct gauge between the rails
options.D: Join two rails together at a joint

e: Creep is the longitudinal movement of rails in the track under traffic and temperature effects; anti-creep anchors grip the rail and bear against the sleepers, resisting this movement and keeping the rail in position.

q: During the monsoon, vulnerable portions of the line and important bridges are kept under special watch by:

options.A: The travelling ticket examiners on duty trains
options.B: The staff of the stores depots
options.C: Patrolmen and watchmen posted for the purpose
options.D: The contractors executing works in the section

e: During the monsoon, vulnerable lengths of line and important bridges face risks from floods and breaches, so patrolmen and watchmen are specially posted to keep watch and report any danger to traffic in time.

q: A Track Recording Car run over a section measures and records:

options.A: The track geometry parameters, such as gauge, alignment, level and twist, for assessing the quality of the track
options.B: The number of passengers travelling in the trains
options.C: The earnings of the stations on the section
options.D: The condition of the rolling stock running on the section

e: The Track Recording Car runs over the section and continuously measures and records track geometry parameters such as gauge, alignment, level and twist, enabling assessment of track quality and planning of maintenance.

q: Training to the civil engineering officers of the Railways in track and works matters is imparted at the:

options.A: National Academy of Indian Railways, Vadodara, in all cases
options.B: Railway Staff College
options.C: Zonal Training Schools of each Railway
options.D: Indian Railways Institute of Civil Engineering (IRICEN), Pune

e: IRICEN, Pune is the specialised institute of the Indian Railways for training civil engineering officers in track, bridges and works matters, so such training is imparted there.

q: Railway electrification projects on the Indian Railways are executed mainly through the:

options.A: Construction organisation of each zonal Railway alone
options.B: Central Organisation for Railway Electrification (CORE)
options.C: Rail Vikas Nigam Limited
options.D: State Electricity Boards

e: CORE, the Central Organisation for Railway Electrification headquartered at Allahabad, is the dedicated organisation through which railway electrification projects on Indian Railways are mainly executed.

q: The Indian Railway Stations Development Corporation (IRSDC), which was wound up with effect from 18.10.2021, was set up as:

options.A: A department of the Railway Board
options.B: A wholly-owned subsidiary of the Indian Railways Catering and Tourism Corporation
options.C: A joint venture of the Rail Land Development Authority (RLDA) and IRCON, set up for the redevelopment of stations
options.D: A private company selected through open tender

e: IRSDC was set up as a joint venture of RLDA and IRCON specifically for the redevelopment of railway stations. It was wound up by Railway Board order dated 18.10.2021, and station redevelopment is now executed by zonal railways / RLDA and under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme. (Source: Railway Board order dated 18.10.2021; effective 18.10.2021).

q: IRCON International Limited is a public sector undertaking of the Railways which undertakes:

options.A: Construction projects, in India and abroad, generally on a turnkey basis
options.B: Only the manufacture of signalling equipment
options.C: The catering and tourism services of the Railways
options.D: The audit of railway works expenditure

e: IRCON International is a railway PSU that undertakes construction projects such as railways, highways and buildings, in India and abroad, generally on a turnkey basis.

q: RITES Limited is a public sector undertaking which provides, in India and abroad:

options.A: Security services for railway premises
options.B: Manufacture of passenger coaches
options.C: Operation of suburban train services
options.D: Consultancy services for transport and other infrastructure projects

e: RITES is a railway PSU providing consultancy services for transport and other infrastructure projects - feasibility studies, design and project management - in India and abroad.

q: Part I of the Pink Book (Works Programme) lists the works which are sanctioned by:

options.A: The General Manager under his delegated powers
options.B: The Railway Board
options.C: The Divisional Railway Manager
options.D: The Ministry of Finance

e: Part I of the Pink Book (Works Programme) lists works sanctioned by the Railway Board, that is, works beyond the sanctioning powers of the General Manager, which appear in Part II.

q: The Liability Register, in which the liabilities incurred in connection with works but not yet discharged are recorded, is maintained in the:

options.A: Office of the contractor executing the work
options.B: Stores depot of the division
options.C: Accounts office
options.D: Office of the Station Master

e: The Liability Register records liabilities incurred on works but not yet discharged, such as unpaid bills and commitments; it is maintained in the Accounts office to watch and clear these liabilities.

q: The wing walls provided at the abutments of a bridge serve to:

options.A: Retain the approach embankment and guide the stream towards the waterway of the bridge
options.B: Carry the track over the bridge
options.C: Support the bearings of the girders
options.D: Provide a footpath for the use of the patrolmen

e: Wing walls at a bridge abutment retain the approach embankment on either side and guide the stream smoothly towards the waterway of the bridge, protecting the embankment from scour.

q: Fresh concrete work executed on a work is required to be kept moist by curing for the prescribed period so that:

options.A: The shuttering can be removed the same day
options.B: The surface can be painted immediately
options.C: The contractor's labour remains occupied at the site
options.D: The concrete attains its designed strength properly

e: Curing keeps fresh concrete moist so that the cement continues to hydrate and the concrete develops its designed strength; concrete allowed to dry out early remains weak.

q: A 'W/L' board provided along the track in the approach to a level crossing indicates:

options.A: The point where the level crossing is to be widened
options.B: The point from which the driver of an approaching train must sound the whistle
options.C: The limit up to which wagons may be stabled on the line
options.D: The location of the water column for locomotives

e: The 'W/L' (whistle) board in the approach to a level crossing marks the point from which the driver of an approaching train must sound the whistle to warn road users.

q: In a 'labour contract' for the execution of a work on the Railways:

options.A: The contractor supplies both the labour and all the materials for the work
options.B: The work is executed by departmental labour without any contractor
options.C: The materials are supplied by the Railways and the contractor is engaged only for providing the labour for the work
options.D: The contractor is paid a share of the earnings of the section

e: In a labour contract the Railways supply the materials and the contractor is engaged only to provide the labour for executing the work, being paid for the labour component alone.

q: The 'out-turn' estimates furnished during the course of a financial year represent:

options.A: The likely actual expenditure for the year, assessed from the progress of expenditure up to the time of their preparation
options.B: The budget estimates for the next financial year
options.C: The appropriation voted by Parliament for the year
options.D: The throw-forward liability of works in progress

e: Out-turn estimates are furnished during the year and represent the likely actual expenditure for the year, assessed from the progress of expenditure up to the time of their preparation.

q: The 'Final Modification' stage of the budgetary cycle is intended to:

options.A: Present the Railway Budget to Parliament
options.B: Finally adjust the grant for the current year in the light of the actual progress of expenditure, providing additional funds where needed and surrendering anticipated savings
options.C: Prepare the budget estimates for the next year
options.D: Close the annual accounts of the Railways

e: At the Final Modification stage, the grant for the current year is finally adjusted in the light of actual progress of expenditure - additional funds are provided where needed and anticipated savings surrendered.

q: Volume II of the Indian Railway Financial Code contains the:

options.A: Establishment Code
options.B: Stores Code
options.C: Accounts Code, dealing with the classification of transactions and the maintenance of accounts
options.D: Engineering Code

e: Volume II of the Indian Railway Financial Code is the Accounts Code, laying down the classification of transactions and the manner of maintaining railway accounts.

q: A techno-economic survey of a proposed railway project is carried out in order to:

options.A: Fix the final alignment of the line on the ground
options.B: Prepare the detailed estimate of the project
options.C: Complete the acquisition of land for the project
options.D: Assess the technical feasibility and the economic and financial viability of the proposal, before it is taken up for detailed investigation

e: A techno-economic survey assesses the technical feasibility and the economic and financial viability of a proposed railway project before it is taken up for detailed investigation and estimating.

q: Measurements recorded in a Measurement Book by a junior official are subject to a 'test check' by the next higher official. The object of the test check is to:

options.A: Delay the payment of the contractor's bills
options.B: Re-measure the whole of the work done
options.C: Fix responsibility for slow progress of the work
options.D: Verify, by sample checking, that the measurements recorded are correct

e: Test check of measurements is a sample verification by the next higher official of measurements recorded by a junior official, to ensure that the recorded measurements - on which payments rest - are correct.

q: When stores are issued from a stores depot for use on a work, an addition is made to their book value to cover the cost of procurement, inspection, storage and handling by the stores organisation. This addition is known as:

options.A: Departmental charges
options.B: D&G charges
options.C: Percentage (overhead) charges on stores
options.D: Agency charges

e: When stores are issued for a work, percentage (overhead) charges on stores are added to their book value to recover the cost of procurement, inspection, storage and handling by the stores organisation.

q: In an EPC contract for a major railway project, the supervision of the work and the certification of the contractor's performance on behalf of the Railways are carried out by:

options.A: The contractor's own project manager
options.B: The tender committee which recommended the award
options.C: The Commissioner of Railway Safety
options.D: The Authority's Engineer appointed for the project

e: In an EPC contract, the Authority's Engineer appointed for the project supervises the work and certifies the contractor's performance on behalf of the Railways.

q: The maximum speed at which a class of rolling stock may be permitted to run on a section is governed by the 'speed certificate' issued by:

options.A: RDSO
options.B: The Commissioner of Railway Safety
options.C: The Railway Board
options.D: The Divisional Railway Manager

e: The maximum permissible speed of a class of rolling stock on a section is governed by the speed certificate issued by RDSO, which certifies the stock as fit for that speed.

q: The Konkan Railway line was constructed and is operated by the Konkan Railway Corporation Limited, which is:

options.A: A division of Western Railway
options.B: A public sector undertaking jointly promoted by the Indian Railways and the States of Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka and Kerala
options.C: A private company promoted by the Government of Maharashtra alone
options.D: A department of the Government of Goa

e: Konkan Railway Corporation Limited is a PSU jointly promoted by the Indian Railways and the participating States - Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka and Kerala - which built and operates the Konkan Railway line.

q: In the case of a newly constructed railway line, the liability to pay dividend on its capital-at-charge is deferred (kept as a deferred dividend liability) during:

options.A: The period of construction only
options.B: The first three years after the line is opened to traffic
options.C: The period of construction and the first five years after the line is opened to traffic
options.D: The first ten years after the line is opened to traffic

e: For a newly constructed line, dividend liability on its capital-at-charge is deferred during the period of construction and the first five years after the line is opened to traffic, and is held as a deferred dividend liability.

q: The Development Fund of the Railways is used mainly for works connected with:

options.A: Track renewals and replacements
options.B: Construction of new lines
options.C: Procurement of rolling stock
options.D: Passenger amenities, staff welfare and unremunerative but necessary operating improvements

e: The Development Fund is used mainly for passenger amenities, staff welfare and unremunerative but necessary operating improvements - works which earn little or no direct return but are needed for better service.

q: In railway works accounts, the term 'allocation' of a work refers to:

options.A: The fund or head of account to which the cost of the work is chargeable, such as Capital, Depreciation Reserve Fund, Development Fund or Revenue
options.B: The contractor to whom the work is allotted
options.C: The division which executes the work
options.D: The year in which the work is commenced

e: 'Allocation' of a work means the fund or head of account - Capital, Depreciation Reserve Fund, Development Fund or Revenue - to which the cost of the work is chargeable.

q: Allotments of funds which are not likely to be utilised during the financial year should be:

options.A: Spent quickly on any available work before the close of the year
options.B: Surrendered promptly, so that the funds can be allotted for other purposes
options.C: Carried forward automatically to the next year
options.D: Transferred to the staff welfare fund

e: Allotments not likely to be utilised during the year should be surrendered promptly, so that the funds can be re-allotted to other works and purposes where they are actually needed.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Funds allotted for a work can be re-appropriated to another work with the sanction of the competent authority.
2. Re-appropriation is permissible only within the same grant; funds cannot be transferred through re-appropriation from a Capital grant to a Revenue grant.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: funds can be re-appropriated between works with competent sanction, but re-appropriation is permissible only within the same grant - funds cannot be moved from a Capital grant to a Revenue grant.

q: Under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, a 'non-local supplier' is a supplier whose goods, services or works have local content of:

options.A: 50 per cent or more
options.B: 20 per cent to less than 50 per cent
options.C: Exactly 20 per cent
options.D: Less than 20 per cent

e: Under the Make in India procurement order, a supplier with local content of less than 20 per cent is a 'non-local supplier'; 20 to less than 50 per cent makes a Class-II and 50 per cent or more a Class-I local supplier.

q: After the tenders for a work have been opened, a tenderer:

options.A: Cannot be permitted to change the substance of his tender
options.B: May freely revise the rates quoted by him
options.C: May withdraw his tender without forfeiture of earnest money
options.D: May impose fresh conditions on his offer

e: After tenders are opened, a tenderer cannot be permitted to change the substance of his tender, as that would disturb the level playing field among tenderers whose offers were opened together.

q: A firm applying for the provision of a private siding is required, at the initial stage itself, to bear:

options.A: The cost of constructing the serving station
options.B: The charges for the survey of the siding and the preparation of its plans and estimate, which are deposited by the applicant
options.C: The cost of the junction arrangements on the main line
options.D: Half of the cost of the land for the siding

e: A firm applying for a private siding must bear, at the initial stage itself, the charges for the survey of the siding and the preparation of its plans and estimate, deposited by the applicant.

q: The correct sequence in the processing of a work for sanction is:

options.A: Expenditure sanction, then administrative approval, then technical sanction
options.B: Technical sanction, then expenditure sanction, then administrative approval
options.C: Administrative approval, then preparation of the detailed estimate and its technical sanction, then expenditure sanction
options.D: Administrative approval, then expenditure sanction, then preparation of the detailed estimate

e: The correct sequence is: administrative approval of the proposal first, then preparation of the detailed estimate and its technical sanction, and finally expenditure sanction authorising the spending.

q: Technical sanction to the detailed estimate of a work is accorded by:

options.A: The Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer
options.B: The Accounts Officer of the division
options.C: The Tender Committee
options.D: The competent engineering authority

e: Technical sanction to the detailed estimate of a work is accorded by the competent engineering authority, which certifies the technical soundness and correctness of the estimate.

q: In working out the anticipated rate of return of a railway project, the 'net gain' is arrived at by deducting from the anticipated gross earnings:

options.A: The working expenses, including maintenance and the provision for depreciation
options.B: Only the dividend payable on the capital-at-charge
options.C: Only the cost of the land required for the project
options.D: Only the cost of the surveys and investigations

e: In working out the anticipated rate of return, 'net gain' is gross earnings minus working expenses, including maintenance and the provision for depreciation, so that only the true net return on capital is measured.

q: Way-leave charges recovered for the use of railway land are credited to:

options.A: Capital of the Railways
options.B: The earnings (revenue receipts) of the Railways
options.C: The Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: Miscellaneous Deposits

e: Way-leave charges are recovered for the use of railway land by others and are credited to the earnings (revenue receipts) of the Railways, since they arise from allowing use of existing land.

q: The value of durable materials brought to the site of a work by a contractor is Rs 6,00,000. The maximum secured advance payable to him against these materials, at 75 per cent of their value, is:
e: Secured advance is payable at 75 per cent of the value of durable materials brought to site: 75/100 x 6,00,000 = Rs 4,50,000.

q: The value of a works contract is Rs 30,00,000. Completion of the work is delayed by 4 weeks for reasons attributable to the contractor. The liquidated damages leviable at 0.5 per cent of the contract value per week amount to:
e:
Liquidated damages per week = 0.5/100 x 30,00,000 = Rs 15,000; for 4 weeks of delay, LD = 15,000 x 4 = Rs 60,000.
Liquidated damages now follow the graduated Clause 17B slabs (0.01-0.05% of contract value per week up to 25% delay, 0.10% for 25-50%, 0.30% above 50%), with a total cap of 5% of the contract value. (Source: GCC for Works, April-2022, Clause 17B (ACS-1 dated 14.07.2022), Railway Board.)

q: A contractor, which is a company, is paid an on-account bill of Rs 10,00,000 for a works contract. Tax deducted at source under Section 194C of the Income-tax Act, at 2 per cent, amounts to:
e: Under Section 194C, TDS on payments to a contractor which is a company is 2 per cent: 2/100 x 10,00,000 = Rs 20,000.

q: The sanctioned estimate of a work is Rs 2.40 crore. On completion, the cost of the work is anticipated to be Rs 2.76 crore. The excess over the sanctioned estimate is:

options.A: Rs 24 lakh
options.B: Rs 36 lakh
options.C: Rs 46 lakh
options.D: Rs 60 lakh

e: Excess over sanctioned estimate = anticipated cost minus sanctioned estimate = 2.76 - 2.40 = Rs 0.36 crore, that is, Rs 36 lakh.

q: The original grant for a work is Rs 500 lakh. A supplementary grant of Rs 60 lakh is obtained during the year, and Rs 25 lakh is re-appropriated from the work to another work. The final grant of the work is:

options.A: Rs 525 lakh
options.B: Rs 545 lakh
options.C: Rs 535 lakh
options.D: Rs 585 lakh

e: Final grant = original grant + supplementary grant - amount re-appropriated away = 500 + 60 - 25 = Rs 535 lakh.

q: A road over-bridge costing Rs 9,00,000 is constructed in lieu of a level crossing on a cost-sharing basis, the cost being shared equally between the Railways and the State Government. The share of the State Government is:
e: The cost is shared equally, so the State Government's share = 9,00,000 / 2 = Rs 4,50,000.

q: A contractor executing a work is required to keep the Contractor's All Risks insurance policy for the work in force until:

options.A: The work is completed and taken over by the Railways
options.B: The first on-account bill of the work is paid
options.C: The Letter of Acceptance is issued
options.D: One month from the commencement of the work

e: The Contractor's All Risks policy must be kept in force until the work is completed and taken over by the Railways, so that the work remains insured against risks throughout its execution.

q: The Revenue Allocation Register maintained in the Accounts office is used to:

options.A: Record the sanctions accorded to estimates
options.B: Check that the expenditure on works and repairs is borne by the correct allocation, such as Capital, Depreciation Reserve Fund, Development Fund or Revenue
options.C: Record the bills passed for payment to contractors
options.D: List the works completed during the year

e: The Revenue Allocation Register in the Accounts office is used to check that expenditure on works and repairs is borne by the correct allocation - Capital, DRF, Development Fund or Revenue.

q: A contract of guarantee, as distinguished from a contract of indemnity, is one in which:

options.A: Only two parties are involved in both cases
options.B: The indemnifier is the principal debtor
options.C: Three parties are involved - the creditor, the principal debtor and the surety - whereas a contract of indemnity involves only two parties
options.D: There is no difference between the two

e: A contract of guarantee involves three parties - creditor, principal debtor and surety, the surety promising to answer for the debtor's default; a contract of indemnity involves only two parties.

q: Where a contractor has executed work under a contract which is subsequently found to be unenforceable, he may claim payment on the principle of 'quantum meruit', which means:

options.A: Payment of liquidated damages by the Railways
options.B: Payment of a penalty for the defective contract
options.C: Payment only at the schedule of rates, without profit
options.D: Payment for the value of the work actually done by him

e: 'Quantum meruit' means payment for the value of work actually done; where the contract proves unenforceable, the contractor who has executed work can claim payment on this principle.

q: In the process of tendering for a work, the Notice Inviting Tender issued by the Railways is, in law:

options.A: An invitation to offer
options.B: An offer
options.C: An acceptance
options.D: A concluded agreement

e: The Notice Inviting Tender is only an invitation to offer: the tenders submitted are the offers, and no contract arises until one of them is accepted by the Railways.

q: The period of limitation for filing a suit for compensation for breach of a contract is:

options.A: One year
options.B: Three years
options.C: Five years
options.D: Twelve years

e: Under the Limitation Act, the period of limitation for a suit for compensation for breach of contract is three years from the date of the breach.

q: The construction organisation of a zonal railway, which executes major projects such as new lines, gauge conversion and doubling, works under the overall control of the:

options.A: Divisional Railway Manager
options.B: Principal Chief Engineer
options.C: Chief Administrative Officer (Construction)
options.D: Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer

e: The construction organisation executing major projects like new lines, gauge conversion and doubling works under the overall control of the Chief Administrative Officer (Construction) of the zonal railway.

q: Major railway projects which are beyond the powers of approval of the Railway Ministry are, before investment approval by the Government, appraised by:

options.A: The Public Accounts Committee
options.B: The Estimates Committee
options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General
options.D: The Public Investment Board

e: Major railway projects beyond the approval powers of the Railway Ministry are appraised by the Public Investment Board before investment approval is given by the Government.

q: A work of improvement which is considered necessary but which does not satisfy the test of financial remunerativeness is ordinarily financed from:

options.A: The Development Fund
options.B: Capital
options.C: The Railway Safety Fund
options.D: Market borrowings

e: A work of improvement which is necessary but does not pass the test of financial remunerativeness is ordinarily financed from the Development Fund, which is meant for such unremunerative but necessary improvements.

q: Works executed by the Railways for other Government departments on a payment basis are:

options.A: Charged to the Capital of the Railways
options.B: Treated as deposit works, with departmental charges levied on them
options.C: Executed free of cost as an inter-departmental service
options.D: Charged to the open-line revenue of the Railways

e: Works executed for other Government departments on a payment basis are treated as deposit works: the cost, with departmental charges levied on it, is recovered from the department concerned.

q: For the acquisition of land for a 'special railway project' under the Railways Act, 1989, the 'competent authority' who carries out the acquisition proceedings is:

options.A: The General Manager of the zonal railway
options.B: The Commissioner of Railway Safety
options.C: An officer notified by the Central Government, ordinarily a revenue officer such as the District Collector
options.D: The Rail Land Development Authority

e: For land acquisition for a 'special railway project' under the Railways Act, 1989, the competent authority is an officer notified by the Central Government, ordinarily a revenue officer such as the District Collector.

q: Under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, an arbitral award made in a dispute arising out of a works contract is required to be:

options.A: A speaking award, that is, an award stating the reasons on which it is based, unless the parties have agreed otherwise
options.B: An award without any reasons in all cases
options.C: Approved by the Railway Board before it is announced
options.D: Pronounced only in the presence of both the parties

e: Under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, an arbitral award must be a speaking award - one stating the reasons on which it is based - unless the parties have agreed otherwise.

q: Road under-bridges provided in lieu of level crossings beneath running tracks are commonly constructed by:

options.A: Open excavation after closing the line to traffic for several weeks
options.B: The box-pushing technique, in which pre-cast RCC boxes are jacked into the embankment under the track
options.C: Tunnel boring machines in all cases
options.D: Dismantling the track and relaying it after construction

e: Road under-bridges in lieu of level crossings are commonly built by box pushing: pre-cast RCC boxes are jacked into the embankment under the track, so traffic on the line is not interrupted for weeks.

q: Where the cant actually provided on a curve is less than the cant required for the equilibrium speed of trains, the shortfall is known as:

options.A: Cant excess
options.B: Negative cant
options.C: Cant deficiency
options.D: Grade compensation

e: Cant deficiency is the shortfall of the cant actually provided on a curve below the cant required for the equilibrium speed - the difference between equilibrium cant and provided cant.

q: On curves, the ruling gradient of a section is eased, that is, made flatter, to offset the additional resistance offered by the curve to the movement of trains. This easing of the gradient is known as:

options.A: Cant deficiency
options.B: Coning of wheels
options.C: Super-elevation
options.D: Grade compensation

e: Grade compensation is the easing (flattening) of the ruling gradient on curves to offset the extra resistance a curve offers to train movement, so the effective gradient remains within the ruling gradient.

q: In railway engineering, the 'formation' of a track refers to:

options.A: The finished surface of the embankment or cutting on which the ballast and the track are laid
options.B: The organisation set up for a construction project
options.C: The plan showing the alignment of a new line
options.D: The profile of the ballast section

e: The 'formation' is the finished surface of the embankment or cutting, prepared to the required level and slope, on which the ballast and track structure are laid.

q: The layer of broken stone or similar material packed under and around the sleepers, which distributes the load of trains to the formation and provides drainage to the track, is called:

options.A: Formation
options.B: Ballast
options.C: Cess
options.D: Shoulder

e: Ballast is the layer of broken stone packed under and around the sleepers; it distributes train loads over the formation, holds the track in position and provides drainage.

q: The 'gauge' of a railway track is:

options.A: The height of the rail section
options.B: The distance between the centres of the two rails
options.C: The clear distance between the inner faces of the two rail heads
options.D: The length of the sleeper laid under the rails

e: The gauge of a track is the clear distance between the inner faces of the two rail heads - 1676 mm for broad gauge - not the distance between rail centres.

q: Amounts paid in advance in connection with capital works, which are pending recovery or adjustment, are held under the Capital suspense head classified as Plan Head:

options.A: 71 - Stores Suspense
options.B: 72 - Manufacturing Suspense
options.C: 73 - Miscellaneous Advances
options.D: 64 - Other Specified Works

e: Amounts paid in advance on capital works and pending recovery or adjustment are held under Miscellaneous Advances, classified under Plan Head 73 of the Capital suspense heads.

q: The Block Account, which forms part of the Finance Accounts of the Railways, primarily shows:

options.A: The monthly earnings of each zonal railway
options.B: The capital-at-charge of the Railways, classified according to the different categories of assets
options.C: The outstanding balances under the various suspense heads
options.D: The loans and advances outstanding against railway employees

e: The Block Account, forming part of the Finance Accounts, shows the capital-at-charge of the Railways classified according to the different categories of assets created out of capital funds.

q: Before the foundations of a major railway bridge are designed, reliable information about the nature, strata and bearing capacity of the sub-soil at the site is obtained by:

options.A: Carrying out bore-hole exploration (geotechnical investigation) at the site
options.B: Examining the oldest bridge in the vicinity of the site
options.C: Referring to the district gazetteer of the area
options.D: Testing the river water for its salinity

e: Before designing foundations of a major bridge, bore-hole exploration (geotechnical investigation) is carried out at the site to obtain reliable information on the nature, strata and bearing capacity of the sub-soil.

q: Unauthorised occupations of railway land noticed by the engineering staff during their inspections are systematically recorded in:

options.A: The Measurement Book of the section
options.B: The Works Register of the division
options.C: The Fixed Asset Register
options.D: The Encroachment Register maintained for the section

e: Unauthorised occupations of railway land noticed during inspections are systematically recorded in the Encroachment Register maintained for the section, so that action for their removal can be pursued.

q: In permanent way terminology, the 'sleeper density' of a track refers to:

options.A: The number of sleepers provided per unit length of the track
options.B: The weight of one sleeper in kilograms
options.C: The depth of ballast provided below the sleepers
options.D: The spacing between two adjacent tracks

e: Sleeper density means the number of sleepers provided per unit length of track (for example, per rail length or per kilometre), which governs how well the load is spread.

q: Fish plates are used in a railway track for the purpose of:

options.A: Fastening the rails to the sleepers
options.B: Preventing the rails from creeping
options.C: Joining the ends of two rails at a rail joint, while allowing for expansion and contraction
options.D: Maintaining the correct gauge between the two rails

e: Fish plates join the ends of two rails at a rail joint, holding them in line and level while still allowing the rails to expand and contract with temperature.

q: In a turnout, the 'stock rail' is:

options.A: The movable rail which directs the wheels from one track to the other
options.B: The fixed outer rail, against which the tongue rail bears when the points are set for a particular direction
options.C: The rail provided inside the running rail to guide the wheel flange on curves
options.D: The short rail connecting the two crossings of a diamond crossing

e: In a turnout, the stock rail is the fixed outer rail against which the tongue (switch) rail bears when the points are set for a particular direction of movement.

q: The tread of a railway wheel is given a slope, that is, coning of wheels is provided, principally so that:

options.A: The wheels can be manufactured easily in the workshops
options.B: The flange of the wheel does not touch the rail on straight track
options.C: The speed of trains can be raised beyond the maximum permissible speed of the section
options.D: The wheelset can shift laterally, enabling the outer wheel to travel a longer distance than the inner wheel on curves and helping the wheelset to remain central on straight track

e: Coning of wheel treads lets the wheelset shift laterally, so on curves the outer wheel rides on a larger diameter and travels farther than the inner wheel; it also helps the wheelset stay central on straight track.

q: In connection with a railway embankment, the term 'cess' refers to:

options.A: The portion of the top width of the formation on either side, beyond the ballast profile, which is used as an inspection path and for stacking materials
options.B: The slope given to the sides of the embankment
options.C: The layer of blanketing material laid over the formation
options.D: The drain running along the toe of the embankment

e: The 'cess' is the portion of the top width of the formation on either side, beyond the ballast profile, used as an inspection path and for stacking materials.

q: A 'momentum gradient' provided on a railway section is:

options.A: The steepest gradient permitted anywhere on the section
options.B: A gradient flatter than the ruling gradient, provided within station yards
options.C: The gradient of the road approach to a level crossing
options.D: A short gradient steeper than the ruling gradient, which a train can negotiate by using the momentum (kinetic energy) gained on the preceding easier stretch

e: A momentum gradient is a short stretch steeper than the ruling gradient which a train can climb using the momentum (kinetic energy) gained on the preceding easier stretch.

q: A 'diamond crossing' in a railway yard is formed where:

options.A: One track branches off from another track
options.B: Two tracks cross each other at an angle, without any provision for a train to pass from one track to the other
options.C: Two turnouts are placed back to back on the same track
options.D: A broad gauge track and a metre gauge track are laid with one common rail

e: A diamond crossing is formed where two tracks cross each other at an angle; unlike a crossover, it provides no means for a train to pass from one track to the other.

q: In earthwork for a railway cutting, a 'spoil bank' is:

options.A: The extra width of land acquired for future widening of the cutting
options.B: A bench cut into the side of a deep cutting for stability
options.C: The stack of serviceable materials released from a work
options.D: The surplus excavated earth which is deposited in a regular heap alongside the cutting or at another approved place

e: A spoil bank is the surplus excavated earth from a cutting, deposited in a regular heap alongside the cutting or at another approved place.

q: A retaining wall is provided in railway earthwork where:

options.A: The earth filling or cutting has to be supported because the natural slope cannot be accommodated within the available width, as in confined or built-up locations
options.B: The height of the embankment exceeds 20 metres in every case
options.C: A road is to be carried over the railway line
options.D: The track passes through a tunnel

e: A retaining wall is provided where earth filling or cutting must be supported because the natural slope cannot be accommodated within the available width, as in confined or built-up locations.

q: Stone 'pitching' is provided on the slopes of railway embankments and cuttings mainly in order to:

options.A: Increase the load-bearing capacity of the formation
options.B: Mark the boundary of railway land on the slopes
options.C: Protect the slopes from erosion by rain and flowing water
options.D: Provide a path for the inspection staff

e: Stone pitching on embankment and cutting slopes protects the slopes from erosion by rain and flowing water, preventing the earth from being washed away.

q: In connection with the protection of bridge foundations, a 'launching apron' is:

options.A: A concrete platform constructed for launching the girders into position
options.B: A thick layer of loose stone provided at the river-bed level around the foundation, which settles and launches itself into the scour hole as scour develops, thereby protecting the foundation
options.C: A temporary staging erected for the inspection of bridge girders
options.D: The raised platform from which the flood levels of the river are observed

e: A launching apron is a thick layer of loose stone laid at river-bed level around a bridge foundation; as scour develops it settles and launches itself into the scour hole, protecting the foundation.

q: The workability (consistency) of freshly mixed concrete used on a work is ordinarily measured at the site by:

options.A: The cube test
options.B: The rebound hammer test
options.C: The ultrasonic pulse velocity test
options.D: The slump test

e: The workability or consistency of fresh concrete is ordinarily measured at site by the slump test, in which the subsidence of a standard cone of concrete is measured.

q: Subject to proper curing, the strength of hardened concrete is governed primarily by:

options.A: The water-cement ratio of the mix, a lower ratio generally giving higher strength
options.B: The colour of the cement used in the mix
options.C: The size of the measuring box used at the mixer
options.D: The speed at which the concrete is placed

e: Subject to proper curing, concrete strength is governed primarily by the water-cement ratio: a lower ratio leaves less excess water and voids, generally giving higher strength.

q: Internal audit in the Railways, as distinguished from internal check, is best described as:

options.A: The continuous checking of transactions which is built into the day-to-day accounting process itself
options.B: The audit of railway accounts conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: The test check of measurements carried out by the engineering officers
options.D: An independent and periodical appraisal, conducted after the transactions have taken place, of the operations and records of a unit or office

e: Internal audit is an independent, periodical appraisal carried out after transactions have taken place, examining the operations and records of a unit or office - unlike internal check, which is built into day-to-day processing.

q: In accordance with the General Financial Rules, tenders invited by Government organisations, including the Railways, are also required to be published on:

options.A: The website of the concerned State Government only
options.B: The Central Public Procurement (CPP) Portal
options.C: The notice board of the nearest district court
options.D: The website of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: Under the General Financial Rules, tenders invited by Government organisations, including the Railways, must also be published on the Central Public Procurement (CPP) Portal to ensure wide publicity.

q: The National Rail Plan (NRP), with a vision horizon of 2030, primarily aims at:

options.A: Privatising the operation of all passenger trains on the Railways
options.B: Fixing the freight rates to be charged for goods traffic
options.C: Preparing the cadre restructuring of railway officers
options.D: Creating railway capacity ahead of demand and increasing the modal share of the Railways in freight transport

e: The National Rail Plan, with a vision horizon of 2030, aims at creating railway capacity ahead of demand and increasing the modal share of the Railways in freight transport.

q: In a 'reverse auction' conducted in e-procurement after the opening of the initial price bids:

options.A: Bidders successively lower their quoted prices online during the auction period, and the lowest bid at the close of the auction is considered for award of the contract
options.B: The contract is awarded to the bidder who had quoted the highest price in the initial bids
options.C: Bidders are permitted to withdraw their earnest money before the auction closes
options.D: The tender is cancelled and invited afresh with revised conditions

e: In a reverse auction after the initial price bids are opened, bidders successively lower their prices online, and the lowest bid at the close of the auction is considered for award of the contract.

q: Before inviting detailed proposals for a complex or public-private partnership project, an 'Expression of Interest' (EOI) is generally invited in order to:

options.A: Award the work without any further tendering
options.B: Fix the earnest money to be deposited by the bidders
options.C: Gauge the interest of the market and shortlist capable parties for the subsequent detailed bidding stage
options.D: Obtain the sanction of the Railway Board for the project

e: An Expression of Interest is invited before detailed proposals to gauge the interest of the market and shortlist capable parties for the subsequent detailed bidding stage of a complex or PPP project.

q: In the context of public-private partnership projects, the abbreviation DBFOT stands for:

options.A: Design, Bid, Finance, Operate and Terminate
options.B: Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer
options.C: Develop, Build, Fund, Own and Transfer
options.D: Design, Build, Furnish, Operate and Tender

e: DBFOT stands for Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer - the PPP model in which the concessionaire designs, builds and finances the project, operates it for the concession period and then transfers it.

q: For a public-private partnership project, 'financial closure' is said to have been achieved when:

options.A: The project has been completed and opened to traffic
options.B: The concession agreement has been registered with the Registrar of Companies
options.C: The first annuity payment has been released to the concessionaire
options.D: The concessionaire has tied up the required debt and equity for the project and the conditions for drawal of the funds are in place

e: Financial closure is achieved when the concessionaire has tied up the required debt and equity for the project and the conditions for drawing the funds are in place, so financing is fully arranged.

q: Under the instructions issued under the General Financial Rules, an Insurance Surety Bond issued by an insurance company is accepted in Government procurement as:

options.A: A valid form of security, in lieu of a bank guarantee, towards earnest money and performance security
options.B: A substitute for the insurance of the work itself
options.C: A security acceptable only for contracts relating to insurance services
options.D: A personal guarantee given by the agent of the insurance company

e: Under the GFR instructions, an Insurance Surety Bond issued by an insurance company is accepted as a valid form of security, in lieu of a bank guarantee, towards earnest money and performance security.

q: In a traditional item-rate works contract on the Railways, the design of the work and the drawings according to which it is to be executed are:

options.A: Prepared by the contractor and got approved after the completion of the work
options.B: Prepared jointly by the contractor and the lowest tenderer
options.C: Furnished by the Railways, and the contractor executes the work in accordance with them
options.D: Prepared by the Tender Committee at the time of acceptance of the tender

e: In a traditional item-rate contract, the design and drawings are furnished by the Railways and the contractor executes the work in accordance with them, being paid at the agreed item rates.

q: Volume I of the Indian Railway Financial Code broadly contains:

options.A: The Accounts Code, dealing with the classification of earnings and expenditure
options.B: The general rules relating to control over expenditure, sanctions, estimates, tenders and contracts
options.C: The rules governing the leave and pension of railway servants
options.D: The classification of stores and the procedure for their purchase

e: Volume I of the Indian Railway Financial Code broadly contains the general rules relating to control over expenditure, sanctions, estimates, tenders and contracts; Volume II is the Accounts Code.

q: A transition curve is provided between a straight length of track and a circular curve in order to:

options.A: Reduce the length of the circular curve
options.B: Enable the rail panels to be welded in the depot
options.C: Provide room for the expansion of long welded rails
options.D: Introduce the curvature and the cant (superelevation) gradually, so that trains pass from the straight to the curve smoothly

e: A transition curve between a straight and a circular curve introduces the curvature and the cant gradually, so that trains pass from the straight onto the curve smoothly without a sudden change.

q: For important structural concrete works, a 'design mix' is adopted, which means that:

options.A: The proportions of the ingredients of the concrete are established through laboratory trials so as to achieve the specified strength and workability
options.B: The proportions of the ingredients are fixed by thumb rule at the site
options.C: Only cement of one particular brand is used in the concrete
options.D: The concrete is designed by the contractor after it has been cast

e: In a design mix, the proportions of concrete ingredients are established through laboratory trials to achieve the specified strength and workability, instead of using fixed nominal proportions.

q: Mechanised tamping of the track is carried out in order to:

options.A: Compact the ballast under the sleepers and restore the correct level and alignment of the track
options.B: Clean the ballast by removing the accumulated fines and dirt
options.C: Grind the rail head to the correct profile
options.D: Detect the internal flaws developed in the rails

e: Mechanised tamping packs and compacts the ballast under the sleepers, restoring the correct level, alignment and cross-level of the track after it has settled under traffic.

q: A buffer stop is provided at the dead end of a siding or a terminal line in order to:

options.A: Indicate the fouling point of the siding
options.B: Support the overhead electrical equipment of the line
options.C: Stop or arrest rolling stock and prevent it from running beyond the end of the track
options.D: Provide a platform for the loading and unloading of goods

e: A buffer stop at the dead end of a siding or terminal line arrests rolling stock and prevents it from running beyond the end of the track.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In hot weather, high compressive thermal stresses build up in long welded rails, and if the resistance of the track is overcome, the track may distort laterally, that is, buckle.
2. In very cold weather, tensile stresses develop in long welded rails, which increases the risk of fracture of the rails.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: in hot weather, compressive thermal stresses in long welded rails can make the track buckle laterally, while in very cold weather tensile stresses develop, increasing the risk of rail fracture.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Schedule of Powers of a zonal railway is framed on the basis of the Model Schedule of Powers issued by the Railway Board.
2. An officer can exercise a delegated financial power only within the monetary limits and subject to the conditions laid down in the delegation.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: a zonal railway's Schedule of Powers is framed on the Model Schedule of Powers issued by the Railway Board, and an officer may exercise a delegated power only within its monetary limits and conditions.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Land acquired for a railway project is got mutated in the revenue records in favour of the Railways.
2. A zonal railway may sell, on its own authority, any railway land which it considers surplus to its requirements.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct - acquired land is mutated in the revenue records in favour of the Railways; statement 2 is wrong, as a zonal railway cannot sell railway land on its own authority.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Catch water drains are provided on the hill side above a cutting to intercept the water flowing down the slope and to divert it away from the cutting.
2. Side drains provided in a cutting run alongside the track and carry the collected water to a suitable outfall.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: catch water drains above a cutting intercept hill-side water and divert it away, while side drains along the track in the cutting carry the collected water to a suitable outfall.

q: The value of durable materials brought to the site of a work by a contractor is Rs 12,00,000. The maximum secured advance payable to him against these materials, at 75 per cent of their value, is:
e: Secured advance at 75 per cent of the value of materials: 75/100 x 12,00,000 = Rs 9,00,000.

q: The value of a works contract is Rs 80,00,000. Completion of the work is delayed by 6 weeks for reasons attributable to the contractor. The liquidated damages leviable at 0.5 per cent of the contract value per week amount to:
e:
LD per week = 0.5/100 x 80,00,000 = Rs 40,000; for 6 weeks of delay, LD = 40,000 x 6 = Rs 2,40,000.
Liquidated damages now follow the graduated Clause 17B slabs (0.01-0.05% of contract value per week up to 25% delay, 0.10% for 25-50%, 0.30% above 50%), with a total cap of 5% of the contract value. (Source: GCC for Works, April-2022, Clause 17B (ACS-1 dated 14.07.2022), Railway Board.)

q: A contractor, who is an individual, is paid an on-account bill of Rs 7,50,000 for a works contract. Tax deducted at source under Section 194C of the Income-tax Act, at 1 per cent, amounts to:
e: Under Section 194C, TDS on payments to an individual contractor is 1 per cent: 1/100 x 7,50,000 = Rs 7,500.

q: The total value of supply under a works contract is Rs 6,00,000, which exceeds the prescribed threshold of Rs 2.5 lakh. The tax deducted at source under the GST law, at 2 per cent, on payment made to the contractor amounts to:
e: GST TDS is 2 per cent of the payment where the supply value exceeds Rs 2.5 lakh: 2/100 x 6,00,000 = Rs 12,000.

q: The sanctioned estimate of a work is Rs 3.60 crore. On completion, the cost of the work is anticipated to be Rs 4.05 crore. The excess over the sanctioned estimate is:

options.A: Rs 40 lakh
options.B: Rs 45 lakh
options.C: Rs 55 lakh
options.D: Rs 35 lakh

e: Excess over sanctioned estimate = 4.05 - 3.60 = Rs 0.45 crore, that is, Rs 45 lakh.
